name: The Sleeping Druid
summary: Oben Rageclaw lies asleep in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, but his spirit is caught in the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine shamans have drawn it from his body and set his flesh moving through the den.

sections.title: A Slumber Disrupted
sections.body: Night elf druids sleep in barrow dens across Kalimdor while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Their bodies rest in stone alcoves, safe through centuries of slumber. Teldrassil's corruption has driven the Gnarlpine furbolgs to desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans found a way to breach Oben Rageclaw's sacred rest and draw his living spirit from his sleeping body.

sections.title: Voodoo and Corruption
sections.body: A Shaman Voodoo Charm, a talisman, lets the Gnarlpine shamans animate Oben's empty body. His spirit is trapped in the Emerald Dream, watching as his flesh stalks the den's corridors and blindly attacks anyone who enters. Oben's spirit asks you to retrieve one of the Gnarlpine charms so he can study it and seek a way to undo the enchantment and restore his body.

aliases: sleeping night elf in barrow den
faq.answer: Oben Rageclaw is a night elf druid who entered a sacred slumber in Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with the Emerald Dream. Hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs took control of his body, leaving his spirit displaced.

faq.q: Why is Oben's body attacking people?
faq.answer: Gnarlpine shamans separated Oben's spirit from his flesh and animated his empty body with dark magic. It now guards the depths of Ban'ethil Barrow Den.

faq.q: What is the Shaman Voodoo Charm?
faq.answer: The Shaman Voodoo Charm is an enchanted focus carried by Gnarlpine shamans in Ban'ethil Barrow Den. They use its dark power to pull sleeping druids' spirits from their bodies and animate their physical husks.

faq.q: Where is Oben's true spirit during the quest?
faq.answer: Oben's spirit is trapped in the Emerald Dream, unable to rejoin his body. Near his resting place, he can communicate with the waking world as a shimmering spirit.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs in Ban'ethil Barrow Den hostile?
faq.answer: Teldrassil's rising taint and madness have turned the Gnarlpine tribe against their former night elf allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have desecrated sacred druidic sites.

faq.q: Can Oben's body be saved without killing it?
faq.answer: Studying the Shaman Voodoo Charm is Oben's first hope of breaking the ritual. By examining the enchantments binding his flesh, he hopes to understand the magic and find a way to resolve the crisis.

angles.text: As a druid, you can see Oben's plight as a waking nightmare: having your body taken while you commune in the Emerald Dream violates the heart of druidic slumber.
As a night elf, you know the Gnarlpine furbolgs' desecration of Ban'ethil Barrow Den marks how far they have fallen from their ancient kinship with the Kaldorei.
